exact_items: Tools.md still treats tool.invoked primarily as analytics data: tool_name, run_id, optional thread_id, latency / success / error
Expand tool.invoked so it can carry runtime attribution on parity with side-effect-relevant tool.denied
Tools.md: stop at tool-specific semantics and reference the shared runtime attribution packet instead of keeping tool events analytics-only
notes: tool.invoked remains under-attributed compared with tool.denied; it must be elevated to first-class runtime trace record carrying the shared runtime attribution packet

exact_items: Define one shared runtime attribution packet and make tool events, artifact envelopes, receipts, and usage records reference it
Contracts_V0.md: own the shared cross-family attribution packet shape for runtime events
notes: One shared attribution family must be available to tool.invoked, tool.denied, runtime_artifact.*, runtime receipts, usage_record, evidence/trace views. Contracts_V0.md should own the cross-family packet shape.

exact_items: runtime artifacts still have no normalized place for attempt_id, node_id, execution_role, provider_attempt_ref, or operational_identity, even though cross-surface receipt linkage already depends on that level of identity
Add attempt/native runtime anchors to the runtime-artifact envelope and artifact index projection
notes: Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md canonical ID set still missing: attempt_id, node_id, execution_role, provider_attempt_ref, operational_identity

exact_items: usage_record is closer to canonical runtime identity than several artifact and tool docs are, but it still keeps old tier_id joins alive
notes: usage_record still carries tier_id joins; these must be retired in favor of attempt_id/node_id/run_id

exact_items: attempt_id remains the canonical local runtime execution anchor
provider_attempt_ref is the canonical bridge to provider/runtime execution details for that attempt
usage_event_ref is the canonical bridge to cost/usage history for that attempt or artifact
receipt records are the canonical bridge to external side-effect lineage for that attempt
Add a bridge-field precedence note to the canonical runtime/storage owner docs
notes: Bridge-field precedence rule: local runtime anchor = attempt_id; provider/runtime bridge = provider_attempt_ref; usage bridge = usage_event_ref; external side-effect bridge = receipt refs. Timestamp/thread fallback routing is compatibility-only.

exact_items: usage-feature.md correctly treats usage_event_ref as canonical when present, but still allows timestamp/run/thread fallback behavior that should probably be treated as degraded compatibility, not the preferred routing path
Treat timestamp/run/thread fallback routing as compatibility behavior only when canonical bridge refs are absent
notes: usage-feature.md should declare timestamp/run/thread fallback as compatibility-mode only, not preferred routing; usage_event_ref is canonical when present

exact_items: Require runtime-artifact envelope support for attempt_id plus bridge refs where applicable
runtime artifacts that are derived from or emitted during an attempt should carry: attempt_id, provider_attempt_ref?, usage_event_ref?, receipt linkage when they summarize external operations
notes: artifact envelopes must carry attempt_id, provider_attempt_ref?, usage_event_ref? to enable cross-surface joins

exact_items: Orchestrator_Page.md still describes worker identity and per-node usage in terms that lag the stronger runtime/account/attempt model
Make cross-surface open actions resolve through bridge fields instead of ad hoc feature-local joins
notes: Orchestrator_Page.md worker identity section must be updated to use attempt_id, execution_role, provider_attempt_ref, and effective account/runtime identity
